stem:
Ethylamine and phenylamine are primary amines.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Fig. 4.1

These two compounds are synthesised by different methods.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: Several methods can be used to form ethylamine.
parts.text:
Ethylamine forms when ethanamide, $\text{CH}_3\text{CONH}_2$, is reduced by $\text{LiAlH}_4$.

Write an equation for this reaction. Use $[\text{H}]$ to represent one atom of hydrogen from the reducing agent.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Ethylamine is a product of the reaction of bromoethane with ammonia.

Name the mechanism of this reaction and state the conditions used.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
The reaction in (a)(ii) also forms secondary and tertiary amines.

Suggest the identity of a secondary or tertiary amine formed by the reaction in (a)(ii).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Ethylamine is a weak base.

State the relative basicities of ammonia, ethylamine and phenylamine.

Explain your answer.

least basic most basic

parts.text:
Pure phenylamine, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$, can be prepared from benzene in two steps.

Draw the structure of the intermediate compound.

Suggest reagents and conditions for each step.

parts.stem: Methylamine, $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$, is another primary amine. $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$ can act as a monodentate ligand.

parts.text: State the coordination number of copper in $[\text{Cu}(\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2)_2(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4]^{2+}$.

parts.label: (f)(i)
parts.stem:
$\text{Cd}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ ions form tetrahedral complexes with $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$, $\text{OH}^-$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ ions, as shown in equilibria 1, 2 and 3.

$$\text{equilibrium 1} \quad \text{Cd}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + 4\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2\text{(aq)} \rightleftharpoons [\text{Cd}(\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2)_4]^{2+}\text{(aq)} \qquad K_{\text{stab}} = 3.3 \times 10^6$$

$$\text{equilibrium 2} \quad \text{Cd}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + 4\text{OH}^-\text{(aq)} \rightleftharpoons \text{Cd}(\text{OH})_4^{2-}\text{(aq)} \qquad K_{\text{stab}} = 5.0 \times 10^8$$

$$\text{equilibrium 3} \quad \text{Cd}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + 4\text{Cl}^-\text{(aq)} \rightleftharpoons \text{CdCl}_4^{2-}\text{(aq)} \qquad K_{\text{stab}} = 6.3 \times 10^2$$
parts.text: Give the units of $K_{\text{stab}}$ for equilibrium 1.

parts.label: (f)(ii)
parts.text: Write an expression for $K_{\text{stab}}$ for equilibrium 3.

parts.label: (f)(iii)
parts.text:
A solution of $\text{Cl}^-\text{(aq)}$ is added to $\text{Cd}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ and allowed to reach equilibrium. The equilibrium concentrations are given.

$$[\text{Cd}^{2+}\text{(aq)}] = 0.043\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$$
$$[\text{Cl}^-\text{(aq)}] = 0.072\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$$

Use your expression in (f)(ii) to calculate the concentration of $\text{CdCl}_4^{2-}\text{(aq)}$ in the equilibrium mixture.

parts.label: (f)(iv)
parts.text:
When $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2\text{(aq)}$ is added to $\text{Cd}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$, a mixture of $[\text{Cd}(\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2)_4]^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ and $[\text{Cd}(\text{OH})_4]^{2-}\text{(aq)}$ forms.

Suggest how the $[\text{Cd}(\text{OH})_4]^{2-}\text{(aq)}$ is formed.

parts.label: (f)(v)
parts.text:
$\text{Cd}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ exists as a complex ion, $[\text{Cd}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}\text{(aq)}$.

Identify the most stable and the least stable of the complexes in Table 4.1 by placing **one** tick (✓) in each column.

Explain your answer.
